title: Widows, Orphans, and the Needy
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Widows, orphans, and the needy refers to God’s special concern for those lacking support, protection, provision, or advocacy. Scripture calls God’s people to practical mercy toward those who are easily neglected.
summary: Widows, orphans, and the needy refers to God’s special concern for those lacking support, protection, provision, or advocacy. Scripture calls God’s people to practical mercy toward those who are easily neglected.
christFocus: Jesus Christ reveals God’s compassion for the helpless and needy. Through Him, believers receive mercy and are called to become a people who care for those the world often overlooks.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God identifies Himself as defender of the fatherless and widows. His concern for the vulnerable is not occasional; it is woven throughout Scripture.

Pure religion includes visiting orphans and widows in their affliction. This means faithful worship cannot be separated from practical mercy toward those in need.

The early church had to address the daily care of widows with seriousness and order. Mercy ministry required attention, fairness, leadership, and action.

Scripture also calls families to care for their own where possible. The church should not neglect the needy, and households should not abandon responsibilities God has given.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
The needy can become invisible when churches focus only on programs, platforms, or those who appear strong. This doctrine calls God’s people to see and serve those who may not be able to repay them.

It also guards against empty religion. A person may speak doctrine correctly while neglecting mercy that God commands.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Look for people who lack support, provision, or protection. Pray, give, visit, advocate, organize help, and serve with humility. Do not wait for the vulnerable to become visible to you; learn to notice whom God calls His people to remember.
